ev.q: First Reported U.S. Cases of Tinea Caused by Trichophyton indotineae — New York City, December 2021–March 2023
a New York City dermatologist notified public health officials of two patients who had severe tinea that did not improve with oral terbinafine treatment

public_health_question.v: What were the clinical features, laboratory identification and treatment course of the first two reported U.S. cases of tinea caused by Trichophyton indotineae?

ev.q: T. indotineae infections have been reported throughout Asia and in Europe and Canada but have not previously been described in the United States
First Reported U.S. Cases of Tinea Caused by Trichophyton indotineae
The cases in these two patients highlight several important points.
Dermatologists noted large, annular, scaly, pruritic plaques over the neck, abdomen, pubic region, and buttocks

equity.level_reason: A two-patient case report; age and sex only describe the patients and no social-position dimension is compared or framed.

ev.q: Patient A, a woman aged 28 years, developed a widespread pruritic eruption during summer 2021.
Patient B, a woman aged 47 years with no major medical conditions

notes: Two-patient case report; Sanger sequencing of the ITS region confirms species identity only and is not a procedure. Outcome types left empty because no quantities beyond case descriptions are reported.
